title: Statement of Work
content:
Statement of Work - Project Phoenix
AI-Powered Customer Service Platform
Client: LanPhilAlex & Miller Retail Group Ltd
Prepared by: Accenture
Document version: 1.3 | Status: Signed | Date: 9 May 2025
1. Engagement Overview
LanPhilAlex & Miller Retail Group ('the Client') has engaged Accenture to design, build, and deploy an
AI-powered customer service platform (internally codenamed 'Project Phoenix') that unifies chat and voice
customer contact channels, integrates with existing order management and loyalty systems, and deflects Tier-1
contact volume away from the Client's human contact-centre agents while improving resolution speed for
customers.
2. Scope of Services
• Design and build a conversational AI bot supporting web chat and voice (via Amazon Connect), covering order
status, returns/refunds, and general product Q&A intents.
• Build a data integration layer unifying customer, order, and product data from the Client's legacy systems into a
platform-native data store.
• Deliver an agent desktop interface enabling human agents to view conversation history and receive
AI-assisted handoffs.
• Deliver a change management and training programme for contact-centre agents and store colleagues.
• Support User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and go-live cutover.
3. Out of Scope
Any capability not explicitly listed in Section 2 is out of scope for this Statement of Work, including (without
limitation) product recommendation or personalised merchandising features. Such items may be delivered
under a separate Change Request following the change control process defined in Section 7.
4. Timeline & Phases
Phase Weeks Key Deliverables
Discovery & Design 1-4 Solution architecture, data mapping, UX designs
Build Sprint 1 5-8 Core bot intents, data pipeline foundations
Build Sprint 2 & Integration 9-12 MVP delivery, system integration, load testing
Testing, UAT & Go-Live 13-16 UAT, training rollout, cutover, hypercare
5. Roles & Governance
Accenture will provide a Project Lead responsible for day-to-day delivery, reporting to an Engagement Partner
who holds overall account accountability. Weekly status reports will be issued to the Client's Executive Sponsor.
A monthly Steering Committee will review progress, risks, and any change requests. A RAID log will be
maintained by the Project Lead and reviewed at each Steering Committee.
6. Commercial Terms

7. Change Control
Any request to modify scope, timeline, or deliverables must be raised as a Change Request, jointly assessed for

title: Solution Architecture (HLD)
content:
Solution Architecture - High Level Design
Project Phoenix - AI-Powered Customer Service Platform
Author: Aisha Rahman & Priya Shah
Document version: 0.8 (draft)
Date: 3 June 2025
1. Component Overview
Component AWS Service Purpose
Voice channel Amazon Connect Inbound/outbound voice, call recording, IVR
Dialogue & intent mgmt Amazon Lex Coarse intent classification, slot filling for the top-8
trained intents
Generative / complex query
handling
AWS Bedrock Foundation model for intents outside the top-8, RAG
over knowledge base
Knowledge base retrieval Amazon OpenSearch + S3 Vector store for FAQ / policy content used in RAG
Orchestration API Gateway + Lambda Routes messages between Lex, Bedrock, and data
layer
Data store DynamoDB Customer360, Orders, ConversationLog tables
Agent desktop React (custom) Human agent UI for handoffs and conversation history
2. Data Flow - Simple Intent
Customer message arrives via web widget or Connect → Lex classifies intent (one of top-8 trained intents, e.g.
order status) → Lambda orchestrator performs slot filling → DynamoDB lookup (Orders / Customer360) →
templated response returned to customer. Typical round trip target: under 1.5s.
3. Data Flow - Complex / Generative Intent
Customer message falls outside the top-8 trained intents → Lambda orchestrator retrieves relevant
knowledge-base chunks from OpenSearch → conversation context + retrieved chunks passed to Bedrock →
generated response returned to customer, with a confidence/sentiment check that may trigger escalation to a
live agent via the /handoff endpoint. Target p95 round trip: 3.5s.
4. Non-Functional Requirements
• Performance: p95 response latency ≤ 3.5s for generative path, ≤ 1.5s for simple intent path.
• Availability: 99.5% uptime for customer-facing endpoints during contact-centre operating hours.
• Security: PII fields (email, address, payment references) encrypted at rest and in transit; access via
least-privilege IAM roles.
• Data residency: all customer data stored within UK/EU AWS regions.
• Scalability: architecture must sustain Black-Friday-equivalent peak concurrency without manual intervention.
5. Open Items
Recommendation engine capability is not represented in this architecture and is not currently in scope (see
Statement of Work, Section 3). Should this be approved via change control, an additional personalisation
service and product-affinity data model would need to be scoped separately.

title: Status Report: Week 11
content:
Project Phoenix - Weekly Status Report
Reporting period: Week 11 (w/c 28 Jul 2025)
Prepared by: Maria Osei, Project Lead
Date issued: 1 August 2025
Distribution: Client Steering, Accenture Account Leadership
Overall RAG: Amber
Workstream RAG Status
Conversational AI Amber
Data & Integration Amber
Change & Adoption Green
Key Achievements This Period
• MVP delivered end of Week 10 as planned.
• Full-scale load testing completed against production-representative volumes.
• UAT scripts drafted for core flows (order status, returns).
• Training materials v1 complete, change readiness survey round 2 launched.
Risks & Blockers
• Performance issue identified in load testing: p95 response latency for Bedrock-backed intent classification
measured at 6.2s against a 3.5s target. Root cause under investigation, fix targeted before the CTO demo on 13
Aug. This is currently the single biggest risk to the demo date.
• Data quality issue found in legacy order-history extract (~8% duplicate customer records), being remediated,
targeted complete 8 Aug. Does not block the CTO demo but adds pressure to the UAT start date.
• Alex Turner (Data Engineer) on leave from Week 10; no confirmed backfill before Week 13. Team is prioritising
ruthlessly to protect critical-path work.
• Marketing's request to add a product recommendation capability remains under review with the client PM; not
yet approved via change control.
Focus for Next Period
• Land and regression-test the latency fix (target: 11 Aug).
• Complete data cleansing to unblock UAT start.
• Finalise and rehearse CTO demo script.
• Confirm interim resourcing options for Data & Integration.

Rachel asked directly: "Will we be ready for the 13th?" Maria's response: high confidence in the demo script and underlying functionality, medium confidence specifically on the latency fix landing with enough time to regression test - team is targeting a fix by 11 Aug, which leaves a 2-day buffer.

Priya explained the ~8% duplicate customerId issue found in the legacy order-history extract, root-caused to a historical merge of two loyalty programmes. Cleansing is in progress (target 8 Aug) and does not block the CTO demo, but does put pressure on the UAT start date. title: Meeting Notes: Architecture Review
content:
PROJECT PHOENIX - ARCHITECTURE REVIEW (INTERNAL)
Wednesday 30 July 2025, 11:00-12:00 BST | Teams call

Attendees:
- Aisha Rahman - Workstream Lead, Conversational AI (chair)
- Priya Shah - Workstream Lead, Data & Integration
- Jordan Reyes - Bot Developer
- Liam O'Connor - Integration Engineer
- Fatima Al-Sayed - Data Quality Analyst
- Sarah Kowalski - NLU/Intent Classification Engineer (first 20 min only)

Purpose: root-cause the latency issue found in Week 11 load testing and align on data quality remediation plan.

1. Latency root cause (Jordan / Sarah)
Load test results: p95 response time 6.2s against a 3.5s target, consistent across three test runs. Sarah walked through the current RAG pipeline - customer message goes to Lex for coarse intent, then for anything outside the top-8 trained intents, the full conversation context plus a knowledge-base retrieval chunk gets sent to Bedrock. The retrieved context chunk has grown over the build (currently averaging ~2,800 tokens) as more FAQ content was added without pruning. Group agreed this is the primary suspect, alongside cold-start latency on the orchestrator Lambda when traffic is bursty.

title: Meeting Notes: Architecture Review
content:
Agreed actions:
- Jordan + Sarah: trim retrieval to top-3 most relevant chunks + summarise long chunks before adding to context (PHX-119)
- Jordan: move orchestrator Lambda to provisioned concurrency for the demo window to eliminate cold starts (PHX-118)
- Liam: confirmed DynamoDB read latency is not a material contributor (<200ms of the 6.2s), ruled out as root cause
- Re-test load scenario by end of day Monday 4 Aug, results to Aisha + Maria before Tue standup

Sarah left the call after this item to get back onto demo-prep work with Aisha.

2. Data quality findings (Fatima)
Fatima presented the reconciliation results: approximately 8% of customerId values in the legacy order-history extract are duplicated, traced to a 2021 merge of two historical loyalty programmes that assigned new IDs without deprecating the old ones. This wasn't visible in the Week 8 sample data (which happened to be drawn from post-merge records only) - it only surfaced once the full 3-year extract was reconciled in Week 10-11, which is why the Week 8 status report shows Data & Integration as Green and the Week 11 report shows Amber.

title: Meeting Notes: Architecture Review
content:
Agreed actions:
- Fatima: build a dedup/merge rule keyed on email + original loyalty number, target complete by 8 Aug (PHX-104)
- Priya: confirm with client data owner whether historical order value should be summed or take-latest on merge
- Group agreed this does not block the CTO demo (demo uses a clean curated dataset) but is on the critical path for UAT start

3. AOB
Liam raised that with Alex out and no confirmed backfill, he and Ravi are absorbing pipeline monitoring on top of their existing tickets (PHX-105) - flagged as a risk to sustaining pace post-demo, not just pre-demo. Priya to keep escalating.

content:
Testing Strategy - Project Phoenix
AI-Powered Customer Service Platform
Author: Priyanka Nair, QA Engineer
Document version: 1.1
Date: 15 June 2025
1. Test Levels
Level Owner Approach
Unit testing Engineers (per workstream) Automated, run in CI on every commit
Integration testing Jordan Reyes / Liam O'Connor Automated suite covering Lex-Lambda-DynamoDB
and Bedrock RAG paths
Performance / load
testing
Jordan Reyes Simulated peak-hour and Black-Friday-equivalent
concurrency against UAT env
Security testing Client InfoSec + Accenture Penetration test + PII handling review prior to go-live
UAT Priyanka Nair (facilitator), client
contact-centre agents
Scripted scenarios plus exploratory testing, Weeks
13-14
2. UAT Plan
UAT will run across Weeks 13-14 with a panel of 8 contact-centre agents and 2 store colleagues, covering order
status, returns/refunds, and escalation-to-human scenarios. UAT start is dependent on completion of the legacy
data cleansing effort (target 8 Aug) so that agents are testing against reliable data.
3. Go-Live Exit Criteria
• p95 response latency ≤ 3.5s sustained across a full load-test cycle.
• Zero open P1 (Highest priority) defects; P2 defects have an agreed workaround.
• UAT sign-off received from client UAT lead.
• Rollback plan documented and dry-run tested.
• Agent training completion ≥ 90% across in-scope contact-centre teams.
• InfoSec sign-off on PII encryption approach.

title: Change Management Plan
content:
Change Management Plan - Project Phoenix
Adoption, training, and communications approach
Author: Marcus Webb / Emma Clarke
Document version: 1.2
Date: 10 June 2025
1. Adoption Timeline
Phase Weeks Activity
Awareness 1-4 Kickoff comms, stakeholder briefings
Preparation 5-10 Training content development, change readiness surveys
Readiness 11-14 Agent training delivery, UAT participation, pilot store briefings
Go-Live & Reinforcement 15-16 Go-live comms, floor support, post-launch survey
2. Training Approach
Contact-centre agents receive a 2-day blended training programme covering the agent-assist desktop,
escalation handling, and conversation history review. Store colleagues involved in the pilot receive a condensed
half-day briefing. Training completion is tracked against a 90% target as part of go-live exit criteria.
3. Communications Schedule
• Week 1: Kickoff email to all contact-centre and store colleagues introducing Project Phoenix.
• Week 8: Midpoint update - what's changing and why, addressing early questions/concerns.
• Week 12: Change readiness survey round 2 (in flight) to gauge sentiment ahead of go-live.
• Week 15: Go-live announcement with clear support channels.
• Week 17 (post-launch): Survey to capture agent feedback and adoption blockers.
4. Change Readiness Risk
Early survey feedback flagged some concern among contact-centre agents that the agent-assist tool could be
perceived as a monitoring/performance-management tool rather than a support aid. Comms and training
materials have been adjusted to explicitly address this, and it is being tracked as an open risk (see RAID log,
R6).
